steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Mix the ground beef, onion, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Mix in the beer until absorbed by the meat mixture. Form into patties.

Cook on the preheated grill until the burgers are cooked to your desired degree of doneness, about 5 minutes per side for well done. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

review.reviewBody: I've been making this recipe for years and it's always been a hit. The only changes that I made was to omit the salt and sometimes use thyme and/or steak spice. I also add 1 egg so that the patties stay glued together while on the grill. Thanks for sharing.

Great hamburger! I love grilling with beer. I used about 1 & 1/4 lbs. of ground beef and about 1/4 cup of finely chopped onion along with the garlic. I kept the other measurements the same (1 Tbsp. of Worcestershire & 1/4 c. beer). There's never a shortage of beer in this house so we used Michelob Ultra. I think any type of full bodied beer will work fine in this recipe. Instead of a tsp. of salt and 1/4 tsp. of pepper I used 1 & 1/4 tsp. of McCormick's Montreal Steak Seasoning. After mixing the ground beef, we let it set for a half hour in the fridge before making the patties to let the flavors come together. These burgers came out very moist and juicy -perfect on a toasted sesame seed roll with melted cheese, lettuce and tomato.

Yum! These burgers were super. I used 93/7 ground turkey instead of beef, the meat mixture did seem very thin and I was worried that these wouldn't hold together well on the grill so I added about 1/4 cup of bread crumbs. Topped with extra sharp white cheddar and served on a hawaiian roll. Thanks for the recipe, we will be making these often!
took forever to cook and was too watery

i have used this recipe several times; most recently with turkey burgers. it is really good. with the turkey burger i melted some butter in some vegetable oil to keep the turkey burger from going dry and mixed some pepper jack cheese in the burger mix. the melted cheese within the burger was really good.

Really good, but I did modify it. I added an egg, breadcrumbs and steak spice as per other reviewers. Texture is amazing, and I am experienced working with very soft burger meat as I make mine with cream cheese and they also are hard to form patties. Just slap the glob on a plate and put it in the fridge for an hour. :)

Delicious! I added an egg because so many folks said they were falling apart and they turned out wonderfully! I used a stout Guinness and it added such amazing flavor. I made these for guests and they loved them! Will definitely make again!
Love this recipe! I used minced onions & garlic salt instead of chopped garlic & regular salt! Came out great! Plus I used my oven broiler because it was raining outside.

This was just OK. Used ground turkey, as we don't eat beef. Added an egg and reduced the beer to 1/8 cup. They were still runny, so added 1/4 cup panko crumbs. Cooked them on the stovetop and glad I did as they never would have stayed together on the grill. If I fix them again, I will add some chipotle peppers or red pepper flakes to jazz it up.

This very similar to a recipe I have used for quite some time. Only difference is I use an IPA or a Porter for the beer. Also, instead of salt and pepper I use Cosco's Sweet Mesquite seasoning. Really adds a nice smokey taste to the burgers.

I think it was too much beer, the burger was too tender. I made this three ways I took the 1/4 of beer and put it in a pot and cooked it down to 1 Oz. this still gave the full flavor of the beer, but still made the beef patty tender. I also used 1 oz of dark German beer and a good Belgium beer. The left over beer I drank, I hate waste.
Absolutely amazing, added egg yolk to keep meat together and maybe added a little too much onion but definitely keeping this one in the books.
this is my go to recipe for burgers. I like to use bison as well. I usually double it too! nice and juicy burgers
Yummy! We topped with pancetta and cheese. :)
I made these burgers and substituted reg milk for the condensed and the burgers were the juiciest we have ever made. I will most definitely make them again.

Looking to kick up the usual - tired of the same old thing - burgers. This one popped up early in the search; looked easy and sounded like it'd be worth giving it a try. How can you go wrong with beer and beef???? Any how, they turned out FANTASTIC!!!! Added some nice fatty bacon & Swiss cheese to a few if them and in the old Emeril talk, BAM......BAM...BAM....... (how many times & ways can one say Fantastic ....Outstanding........ about a burger ??) Another keeper - and an added note - I've tried a number & variety of recipes from the AllRecipes site and not one has missed the mark as of yet - so I think AllRecipes is a KEEPER TOO!!!

I never would have thought of adding beer to my burgers, but what a great addition it is. The burgers were super tender! I used Montreal Steak Seasoning instead of salt and pepper. 
The only problem, as others mentioned, is that these burgers tend to fall apart. I added both an egg and some breadcrumbs, and refrigerated the formed patties for half an hour, and my husband still said they were hard to handle on the grill. But the flavor was superb.
A very moist hamburger with great flavor. A favorite at our family barbeques.
I made this it was good I just tweeked it a bit I also added half pound ground pork 2 egg and 1cup bread crumbs. Very good lots of compliments

Got a little excited that I was using beer in burgers and put a little too much lol but squeezing them a little before shaping helped. They're a little hard to work with but came out amazingly delicious and almost put the smack down on the old man for the last one. Definately a keeper.
